agent._: What a session runs under when its creator does not say.
agent.permission_mode: Who answers when a session asks to reach past its confinement when neither you nor its agent profile chooses a mode.

attachments._: What a file you attach may cost the conversation it rides in.
attachments.inline_image_megabytes: The ceiling on an image inlined for a vision model. Above it the path and metadata still reach the model, but the pixels do not.

composio.enabled: Expose Composio's hosted gateway as one MCP server.
composio.url: The hosted MCP URL from the Composio dashboard's "connect" page.
composio.api_key: The API key shown beside that URL. COMPOSIO_API_KEY wins over this.
composio.server_name: The MCP server name its tools appear under.
composio.timeout_seconds: How long one call to that gateway waits.

computer_control.enabled: Let the agent drive native applications and your browser. It also needs Accessibility granted in System Settings.

retrieval._: Which models rank a screen, and when a query's spelling stops being evidence.
retrieval.multilingual_rank_model: The static embedding that ranks by meaning across languages. Also the model whose plain cosine backs the relevance floor, so clearing it disables that floor. Empty turns it off.
retrieval.english_rank_model: A second static embedding, ranked alongside the first rather than instead of it. Stronger on queries that describe what an element is for; weaker on exact labels. Empty turns it off.
retrieval.lexical_gate_short_words: Queries of this many words or fewer are treated as a label quoted off the screen, and the character similarity counts in full.
retrieval.lexical_gate_long_words: Queries of this many words or more are treated as a description of a purpose, and the character similarity is ignored — its spelling agrees with nothing, so it ranks by coincidence.

dictation._: Speaking to the composer instead of typing.
dictation.enabled: Let the composer take speech. The model runs on this machine.
dictation.model: The speech model dictation downloads and runs locally.

timing._: How long dictation waits before it gives up.
timing.minimum_transcription_timeout_seconds: The floor on how long one transcription may take before it is treated as wedged.
timing.transcription_timeout_realtime_multiplie: Added to the floor, per second of audio. Transcription runs comfortably faster than real time on Apple Silicon, so reaching the limit means stuck, not busy.
timing.maximum_attempts: How many workers one recording may be given.
timing.worker_shutdown_seconds: How long a worker is given to exit on its own before it is killed.

email._: IMAP IDLE plus SMTP in front of this daemon. A new thread addressed to local+machine@domain starts a session here; a reply steers that conversation.
email.enabled: Run the mail client against this mailbox.
email.address: The mailbox. IMAP logs in as the account; SMTP From uses local+machine@domain so replies stay tagged.
email.machine: This host's plus-tag. New threads must be addressed here; replies follow the thread even if the tag is missing.
email.allow_from: Mailboxes (or @domain) whose mail is taken. Everyone else is ignored.
email.agent: The agent profile each mail thread session runs.
email.provider: Optional catalogue provider overlay for mailbox sessions. Set together with email.model.
email.model: Optional catalogue model overlay for mailbox sessions. Set together with email.provider.
email.auth: How IMAP and SMTP authenticate: password or oauth.
email.working_directory: Where mail sessions' tools run. Empty leaves the daemon's current directory.
email.permission_mode: Who answers gates for a mail session.
email.idle_timeout_seconds: How long one IMAP IDLE waits before cycling.
email.turn_timeout_seconds: How long to wait for this mail's turn before giving up.

oauth._: OAuth2 for IMAP/SMTP. Tokens live as secret files.
oauth.issuer: google, microsoft, yahoo, or custom. Empty infers from the address.
oauth.token_url: Token endpoint, for a custom issuer.
oauth.authorize_url: Authorize endpoint, for a custom issuer.
oauth.redirect_uri: Loopback URI langmesh mail auth listens on.
oauth.client_secret: Unused in YAML. The live secret is the file email.oauth.client_secret.
oauth.refresh_token: Unused in YAML. The live secret is the file email.oauth.refresh_token.

imap._: The mailbox the mail client IDLEs on.
imap.host: IMAP server. Inferred from the address when empty.
imap.username: IMAP login. Empty means the account without a plus-tag.
imap.password: Unused in YAML. The live secret is the file email.imap.password.

smtp.host: SMTP server. Inferred from the address when empty.
smtp.username: SMTP login. Empty means the IMAP username.
smtp.password: Unused in YAML. The live secret is the file email.smtp.password.

exa.api_key: Exa API key. The EXA_API_KEY environment variable wins over this.

firecrawl.api_key: Firecrawl API key. FIRECRAWL_API_KEY wins over this.
firecrawl.api_url: A self-hosted Firecrawl instance to use instead of the hosted API.

jina.api_key: Jina API key, which raises the rate limit. JINA_API_KEY wins over this.

mcp.servers: MCP servers, by name. Edited on the MCP panel, which is where a server's command and credentials belong.

SettingsAbout.providers: Credentials for each model provider. The provider's own environment variable wins over anything stored here.

remote_agents._: Agents on other hosts, read from remote-agents.json.
remote_agents.agents: Remote peers, by name. Edited on the peers panel.

sandbox._: What a session's tool children may do, enforced by the operating system.
sandbox.enforce: What to do on a machine that cannot enforce confinement: refuse to start the session, run with resource limits only, or do not confine.

filesystem._: Which paths a tool child may read and write.
filesystem.readable: Paths under your home a tool child may read. The system is readable and is not listed.
filesystem.writable: Paths a tool child may write. Deliberately narrower than readable, because a wrong write is the failure people actually meet.
filesystem.grantable: Paths an agent may be granted at runtime without asking. Empty means every request is put to you.
filesystem.deny: Opt-in absolute bans that no access request may open. Empty by default.

sandbox.network: Whether a tool child may reach the network at all.
sandbox.limits: Per-child resource limits, by their setrlimit names.
sandbox.umask: The file-creation mask a tool child runs under. Empty leaves the machine's own.
sandbox.nice: How far to lower a tool child's scheduling priority, so a runaway command does not take the machine with it.

exporter.endpoint: Where traces are sent. Empty sends none.
exporter.protocol: The OTLP protocol that collector speaks.
exporter.headers: Headers sent with every export, for a collector that authenticates.

telemetry.sample_ratio: Share of traces exported. 1.0 exports every one.

toolbox._: Whether a session may install the tools it needs into a profile of its own.
toolbox.enabled: Let each session install the tools it needs into a package profile of its own, deleted with the session.

tuning._: How large, how many, and how patient the tools are.

limits._: Set any tunable by its own name. Every duration is in seconds and every value is used exactly as written.
limits.accessibility_messaging: How long one accessibility message to an application waits, so a hung application costs a moment rather than the whole action.
limits.accessibility_prewarm_interval: Pause between pre-warming the frontmost application's accessibility tree.
limits.accessibility_ready_backoff: Ceiling on the widening pause between accessibility readiness probes.
limits.accessibility_ready_probe: How long the readiness poll may spend deciding whether an app's tree has built yet. Short on purpose: it runs repeatedly while an app is still starting, and it only has to see past the window chrome.
limits.accessibility_walk_budget: How long one read of an app's accessibility tree may take.
limits.action_timeout: How long one browser action (click, type, hover) waits for its element.
limits.bash_sync_window: How long a shell command runs inline before it moves to the background. It is not killed at this point, only handed off, and the model can override it per call.
limits.browser_authorization: How long attaching waits for the user to approve Chrome's prompt.
limits.card_resolve: How long fetching a remote agent's card waits.
limits.control_script: How long one screen-control script may run.
limits.credential_refresh_leeway: How far ahead of its expiry an access token is refreshed.
limits.drag_step_interval: Pause between the interpolated steps of a drag.
limits.drag_steps: Segments a drag is split into, so it looks like a hand moved it.
limits.drag_timeout: How long a drag between two elements waits.
limits.fetch_tokens: Tokens of a fetched web page's text kept inline.
limits.file_url_ttl: How long a signed file URL stays valid.
limits.find_anchor_margin: How far ahead of its own runner-up a near= anchor must score before a find will join on it.
limits.find_candidates: Elements find_one weighs against its best match, and offers back when it cannot choose between them.
limits.find_many_ceiling: Elements find_many will return however many are asked for.
limits.find_near_weight: How much sitting beside the anchor is worth against matching the query, when a find names one with near=.
limits.find_one_margin: How far ahead of the runner-up find_one's best match must score, in units of the shortlist's own spread, before it answers with one element instead of asking which was meant.
limits.find_relevance_floor: How well an element must match, as a cosine against the query, before find_many will return it at all. It cuts the noise band and nothing more.
limits.find_rephrasing_similarity: How alike two screen queries must be, as a cosine in the retrieval model's own space, before a second one landing on the same element counts as the first asked again.
limits.focus_settle: Pause after focusing a field, before typing into it.
limits.frame_resolve_timeout: How long resolving a frame reference waits. Deliberately well below the action timeout: a frame that has gone waits out its budget rather than erroring, and listing every frame would otherwise stall on the one that left.
limits.mcp_connect: How long connecting to one MCP server waits.
limits.model_catalogue_ttl: How long the list of available models is cached.
limits.model_silence_give_up: How long a model may hold a stream open saying nothing at all before the turn is ended. Long, because a model weighing a hard problem is silent and still working.
limits.navigation_timeout: How long a page load or navigation waits.
limits.oauth_poll_ceiling: Ceiling on the widening pause between sign-in polls, so a slow sign-in is not asked about every second for minutes.
limits.oauth_poll_give_up: How long a browser sign-in is waited for before it is abandoned — a person's whole trip through a consent screen, not a network round trip.
limits.oauth_poll_interval: First pause between asks of whether a browser sign-in has completed; it widens from here.
limits.open_url: How long handing a URL to the system browser waits.
limits.output_tokens: Tokens of inline output one tool may return before the rest overflows to a file.
limits.permission_reviewer_attempts: How many times the permission reviewer is asked before its silence counts as a refusal.
limits.read_text_timeout: How long reading a page's text waits.
limits.scroll_amount_pixels: Pixels one scroll step moves a native window.
limits.session_title_attempts: How many times a session asks the model to name itself before giving up.
limits.settle_stable_reads: Identical consecutive reads that count a surface as having stopped changing.
limits.settle_poll_seconds: How often to re-check whether a screen surface has settled after an action.
limits.settle_give_up_seconds: The longest to wait for a screen surface to settle before reading it anyway.
limits.sigterm_grace: How long a cancelled command or a reaped session has after SIGTERM before SIGKILL.
limits.slow_tool_sync_window: The same inline window for fetching a URL or downloading a file.
limits.snapshot_timeout: How long an accessibility snapshot of a page waits.
limits.subscription_resume_ttl: How long a subscription provider's server-side conversation state stays worth resuming from before the whole conversation is resent instead.
limits.surface_guard_margin: How far above the script's own limit the machinery waiting on it sits, so raising that limit can never make the guard fire first and leave the surface half-dead.
limits.type_chunk_size: Characters sent per synthesized keyboard event.
limits.upstream_error_detail_tokens: Tokens of an upstream service's error body kept in the failure this harness raises — enough to carry the provider's own explanation, short of pasting a whole page into a message someone has to read.
limits.web_exchanges: Recent request/response pairs a browser session keeps, so a search can surface the API behind a rendered view.
limits.web_search_maximum: Ceiling on the result count a web search may ask for, however many it requests.
limits.web_search_sync_window: The same inline window for a web search.
limits.web_websockets: Live websockets a browser session tracks at once.

user_context._: Whether model-facing session context describes how you work on this machine.
user_context.enabled: Include a snapshot of how you work — your editor, your habits, your machine — in session context.
user_context.refresh_hours: How old the snapshot may get before it is rebuilt. The rebuild runs in the background, so no message ever waits for it.

web_fetch.download_timeout_seconds: How long a download is given, which is longer than a fetch because it carries the whole file.
web_fetch.minimum_useful_characters: Below this a page is a wall or a stub rather than the content, so the next engine is tried.
web_fetch.proxy_url: Route direct fetches and file downloads through an HTTP or SOCKS proxy, for sites that block by address. Empty fetches directly. Credentials may be embedded as http://user:pass@host:port.
web_fetch.timeout_seconds: How long one reader engine is given before the cascade moves on to the next.

workspace.strategy: Where a session's work happens: the project directory itself, a branch of its own, or a git worktree of its own.

compaction._: How conversation history is compacted as it grows.
compaction.automatic: Compact on its own as the conversation fills. Manual compaction works either way.
compaction.reclaim_at_fraction: Recommended preparation boundary within the usable window. The agent records durable knowledge before older history is discarded, so the reserved space remains available for that final segment.
compaction.output_reserve_fraction: Safety buffer kept outside the usable window for the current answer and the pre-compaction recording segment.
compaction.recent_working_set_fraction: Share of the usable window kept verbatim after older history is discarded. It is measured in tokens because one turn may contain hundreds of tool results.

goal_review._: How a satisfied or blocked mark is settled. A reviewer that stops without a verdict is asked again until it submits.
goal_review.settlement: An independent reviewer confirms or overrides the working agent's mark, or that mark is final and the session ends.

SettingsDialog.firecrawlApiKeyHint: Fallback engine for pages Jina can't render.
SettingsDialog.fullDiskAccessBody: Screen Time and Safari history need Full Disk Access.
SettingsDialog.jinaApiKeyHint: Web fetch works without one; a key raises the rate limit.
SettingsDialog.proxyServerHint: Routes web fetches and downloads through a proxy for IP-blocked sites.
SettingsDialog.restartBody: LangMesh needs to restart for the Accessibility permission to take effect — the daemon re-reads it only on a fresh start. Your sessions are kept: each one loses its process and picks back up where it left off on the next message. Computer control turns on automatically once it does.
SettingsDialog.title: Settings
SettingsDialog.toolboxHint: Let each session install the tools it needs into a profile of its own, deleted with the session.
SettingsDialog.toolboxUnavailable: This machine has no package manager that can give a session tools of its own.
SettingsDialog.userContextHint: Share a snapshot of how you work — frequent folders, recent files, apps, and sites — so the assistant fits your habits. Off by default; stays on this machine.
